classification.difficultyReason: Complete the Venn counts and, for the conditional part, restrict the denominator to English literature students rather than the whole group.

content.prompt: In a group of 100 students, 50 study history, 30 study English literature and 20 study both.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Represent this information on a Venn diagram.

answer.short: Let $H$ represent history and $E$ represent English literature. History only: 30; both: 20; English literature only: 10; neither: 40.
answer.worked:
Let $H$ represent history and $E$ represent English literature. Place 20 in the overlap.

$$\begin{align*}\text{History only}&=50-20=30\\\text{English literature only}&=30-20=10\\\text{Neither}&=100-(30+20+10)=40\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If a student is selected at random from the group, what is the probability that the student studies:

children.label: i
children.prompt: at least one of these subjects?

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Number studying at least one subject}&=30+20+10=60\\P(\text{at least one subject})&=\frac{60}{100}=\frac{3}{5}\end{align*}$$

children.label: iii
children.prompt: history, given that the student also studies English literature?

answer.short:
$\frac{2}{3}$

Of the 30 English literature students, 20 also study history.
answer.worked:
The condition restricts the group to the 30 students studying English literature. Of these, 20 also study history.

$$P(\text{history}\mid\text{English literature})=\frac{20}{30}=\frac{2}{3}$$
